meta.title: Tunelle, a lossless audio player
meta.description: Tunelle is a free, open-source audio player for your own music: lossless files play exactly as recorded on Windows, macOS and Linux.
meta.ogDescription: Free, open-source player for your own music. Windows, macOS and Linux.
hero.title: Your music, exactly as recorded.
hero.lead: Tunelle is a free, open-source player for the music you own. Point it at your folders and it plays lossless files without touching the sound.
hero.meta: Version {{version}} · Windows, macOS and Linux · release notes
hero.alt: The Tunelle window with an album open: the cover, the track list and a FLAC 16/44.1 badge on every track.
chips.label: At a glance
features.title: What you get
features.library.title: Your library, any way you browse
features.library.text: Albums, artists, album artists, genres, songs and folders. Search by artist, album or title, sort every list, and narrow it to the folders you pick.
features.lossless.title: Lossless, and you can see it
features.lossless.text: Every track and station wears its format: FLAC 16/44.1, FLAC 24/96, MP3 320. No guessing what you are listening to.
features.formats.title: Plays what you have
features.formats.text: FLAC, ALAC, APE, WavPack, AIFF, DSD, WMA, MP3, AAC, M4A, Ogg, Opus and WAV, with the tags and the cover read from the files.
features.radio.title: Internet radio built in
features.radio.text: Thousands of stations from the open radio-browser.info directory, with their logos, filters and the song that is on right now. More about radio
features.home.title: A Home that remembers
features.home.text: Pick up where you stopped, replay what you heard last, and start your Liked tracks, a playlist or a favourite station in one click.
features.liked.title: Liked and playlists
features.liked.text: Heart a track, an album or a station and it waits in Liked. Build playlists, reorder them by dragging, and keep playing even when a folder is away.
features.equalizer.title: An equalizer you can see
features.equalizer.text: Ten bands drawn as a curve: drag a dot or pick Bass boost, Vocal, Treble boost or Loudness.
features.queue.title: A queue you control
features.queue.text: Add songs, albums or playlists to the end, or play them next. Drag them into order, or move them with Alt and the arrow keys, and take out what you do not want. Shuffle and repeat are one tap away.
features.theme.title: Light, dark, or your cover
features.theme.text: Follow the system or choose a mode, then pick an accent colour, or let it follow the cover of whatever is playing.
features.language.title: Speaks your language
features.language.text: English and Hungarian, following your system unless you say otherwise.
features.native.title: Feels at home
features.native.text: Media keys and the media controls of your system, play buttons on the Windows taskbar, a menu entry on Linux, and a translucent window that blurs the desktop where the system allows.
features.free.title: Free, private, up to date
features.free.text: No price, no account, no tracking. Artist photos come from Deezer, which is sent the names of your artists, and you can turn that off in Settings; the privacy page lists everything the app contacts. The app updates itself, and new releases come out twice a week, under the MIT licence.
tour.title: A look around
tour.home.title: Open it, and your music is waiting
tour.home.text: Home keeps what you were doing: a button to continue the track you paused, the list of what you played lately and tiles for your Liked tracks, your playlists and your favourite stations. Clear the list whenever you like.
tour.home.alt: The Home page of Tunelle: tiles for Liked and a playlist, the recently played tracks and a station with their formats, and three favourite radio stations with their logos.
tour.albums.title: Every album, front and centre
tour.albums.text: A grid of covers that fills the window, with a slider for the size. Click a cover for the track list, a format badge on each track and a Play album button, and a Change cover button to pick another image from your computer when the cover is wrong; sort by title, artist, year, length or number of tracks.
tour.albums.alt: The albums page of Tunelle: five album covers in a grid with artist, year, number of tracks, length and a FLAC badge, a search box, folder filter, sort menu and a cover size slider.
tour.genre.title: Artists, album artists and genres
tour.genre.text: Browse by who made it or what it is. Genres get a colour and a fan of covers; open one and press Play all or Shuffle to queue everything in it. Open an artist and press Change photo to pick an image from your computer, or to search for another photo, when the photo is wrong.
tour.genre.alt: An opened genre in Tunelle with Play all and Shuffle buttons in the header and the two albums of the genre below.
tour.songs.title: Everything you own, in one list
tour.songs.text: Every file in your folders with its artist, year, album, track number and format. Tick several songs and play just those. Open a folder once and the library keeps itself in step with it: files you add, change or remove show up within about ten seconds, with no rescan, and big libraries and folders on a slow network or removable drive are looked at less often.
tour.songs.alt: The songs list of Tunelle with the title first, the artist, album and year muted beside it, a FLAC badge on every track and the heart, add to playlist, add to queue and play next buttons on the playing row.
tour.folders.title: Drop a folder in, or take one away
tour.folders.text: Drag folders onto the window or pick them, and watch the scan count its files. A copy of a whole album is one scan, not one per file, and you can turn the watching off in the Settings for a slow drive. A folder that is unplugged stays in the library as Unavailable, its tracks and favourites wait for it, and nothing on disk is ever touched.
tour.folders.alt: The folders page of Tunelle: a folder row with Remove, an Add folder button and a drop area.
tour.now.title: What is playing, and what is next
tour.now.text: The cover, the format and the whole queue sit on one page. Add songs, albums or whole playlists to the end of the queue, or play them right after the song that plays; several that you put next play in the order you chose them. Drag them into the order you want (or move a row with Alt and the arrow keys), take out what you do not, or clear the queue, which stops the song as well. The player bar keeps the controls, the position and the volume in reach. Tracks follow each other without a gap, whether the queue is an album, a playlist or a shuffle, and they play at the same loudness when the files carry ReplayGain tags, or when the app has measured them in the background (per track or per album, or off in the settings), and the page shows how the loudness of a measured song is spread, with its loudness, range and peak, and a bar that moves across it as the song plays. In the settings you pick which output device the sound goes to, such as a DAC, headphones or speakers; a device that is unplugged gives way to the system default.
tour.now.alt: The Now playing page of Tunelle: the large cover, the queue of four tracks and the player bar with the progress.
tour.radio.title: Internet radio, next to your own music
tour.radio.text: Search the station directory by name, genre, country, language, codec or bitrate, and sort by popularity, name, bitrate, trending, votes or country, or by clicking a column. Stations show their logo, genres, codec, bitrate and country, a live badge tells you it is a stream, and the player bar shows the song that is on right now, with its cover.
tour.radio.more: The list reflows to a narrow window, dropping the least important columns first.
tour.radio.alt: The Radio page of Tunelle: a table of stations with logos, genres, codec, bitrate and country, filter chips for genre, country, language, codec and bitrate, a sort menu, and a live station playing in the player bar.
tour.liked.title: Heart it, and it is yours
tour.liked.text: Tracks, albums and stations land in one Liked page with a switch between Local and Online, a count of what is in it, Play all and Shuffle. Sort by when you liked it, by name or by artist.
tour.liked.alt: The Liked page of Tunelle: a heart cover with totals, Play all local and Shuffle buttons, a Local and Online switch and a list of liked tracks and albums.
tour.playlist.title: Playlists, the quick way
tour.playlist.text: Press the plus in the sidebar, name it, then add tracks or whole albums from any list. Drag playlists into order and drag the tracks inside one. Tracks whose files are away stay put and play again when they return.
tour.playlist.alt: A playlist in Tunelle named Late night: numbered rows with title, artist, album and format, and a Play all button.
tour.equalizer.title: Shape the sound
tour.equalizer.text: Ten bands from 70 Hz to 16 kHz, drawn as a curve you drag. Presets get you started, Faders show the numbers, Reset puts it flat again.
tour.equalizer.alt: The Equalizer page of Tunelle: the Bass boost preset drawn as a response curve with ten draggable points.
tour.settings.title: Make it yours
tour.settings.text: Light, dark or follow the system. Six accent colours, your own, or an automatic one that follows the cover of the song. Turn on translucent panels where your desktop blurs windows, switch the language, and decide if artist photos may be fetched.
tour.settings.more: The version and the update status live in the same place; the app checks on start and can check on demand, and asks before it downloads an update on a metered connection. A small pill in the title bar lists the background work while there is any, and a notification tells you when a scan added or removed songs while the window is in the background (you can turn it off).
tour.settings.alt: The Settings page of Tunelle: theme mode tiles, accent colours, language, the library folders, the output device, the loudness normalization, a Measure loudness switch with its progress, a Watch library folders switch, an Artist photos switch and a Window blur switch.
tour.light.alt: The albums page of Tunelle in the light theme, with a dark blue accent taken from the cover that is playing.
tour.light.caption: The light theme, with the accent taken from the cover that is playing.
tour.madeUp: The music and the stations in the screenshots are made up for the pictures.
download.title: Download
download.intro: Pick your system. Not sure about the processor? Most computers made in the last years are the first choice of the list.
download.windows.or: Or the installer, which updates itself:
download.linux.recommended: Recommended: it updates with your system. Or the AppImage:
flatpak.title: Linux: install with Flatpak
flatpak.intro: Works on every distribution with Flatpak. The runtime comes from Flathub, the repository of this site is signed, and flatpak update brings every new release.
flatpak.opens: opens GNOME Software or KDE Discover on the install page of Tunelle (the browser may ask first whether to open it). Nothing happened? Your system does not open these links: download the file and open it, or paste this in a terminal, it adds the repository and installs the app:
flatpak.meta: Then start it from the application menu or with flatpak run io.github.koeroesi86.Tunelle. To add only the repository: flatpak remote-add --user --if-not-exists tunelle https://koeroesi86.github.io/tunelle/repo/tunelle.flatpakrepo. The repository holds the latest release; a .flatpak file from the releases page has no repository and does not update, so install it again with the command above.
macos.summary: macOS: how to open Tunelle the first time
macos.move: Open the downloaded .dmg and drag Tunelle to the Applications folder, then start it from there. From the disk image, or from a folder you can not write to, it can not update itself; the settings say so.
macos.gatekeeper: Tunelle is not signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS stops the first start with a message that it can not check the app for malware. Open System Settings, Privacy & Security, scroll down to the message about Tunelle, click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. This is needed once. On macOS 14 and older, right-click Tunelle and choose Open instead.
macos.terminal: Or take the mark of the download off in a terminal: xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/Tunelle.app.
macos.update: From then on it updates itself on start and checks the signature of every update. macOS may ask again for access to your music folders after an update.
appimage.summary: Linux: how to start the AppImage
appimage.glibc: It runs on Ubuntu 22.04 or any newer distribution (glibc 2.35 or newer).
appimage.am: Installed with AM (am -i tunelle) it updates with am -u tunelle and not by itself, and so does an AppImage in a folder you can not write to; the settings say so.
appimage.chmod: Make the downloaded file executable: chmod +x Tunelle-<version>-<arch>.AppImage, or tick "Allow executing as a program" in the file manager.
appimage.start: Start it with ./Tunelle-<version>-<arch>.AppImage or by double click.
appimage.fuse: It needs FUSE 3: the fuse3 package gives the fusermount3 helper, and desktop installs have it. Without FUSE, start it with APPIMAGE_EXTRACT_AND_RUN=1 ./Tunelle-<version>-<arch>.AppImage.
appimage.fuse2: Version 26.10.2 and older also need FUSE 2 (sudo dnf install fuse-libs on Fedora, sudo apt install libfuse2t64 on Ubuntu 24.04).
download.releases: Every file of every release is on the releases page.

privacy.title: Privacy, Tunelle
privacy.description: What Tunelle contacts, what it sends and where its radio stations and covers come from.
privacy.heading: Privacy
privacy.lead: Tunelle has no account, no analytics and no tracking. Your library, playlists, favourites and settings stay on your computer. This page lists the only places the app talks to.
privacy.contacts.title: What the app contacts
privacy.contacts.directory: The station directory, radio-browser.info. The Radio page asks it for stations, with the words and filters you search for, and when you play a station it asks for the address of its stream. Like any request, this shows your IP address to the directory.
privacy.contacts.stations: The stations. A stream and the logo of a station are loaded from the servers of the station, which see your IP address like any web server does.
privacy.contacts.musicbrainz: MusicBrainz and the Cover Art Archive. When a station announces a song but gives no cover for it, the title of the song is sent to MusicBrainz to find the release it is on, and the cover is loaded from the Cover Art Archive. The cover is kept in memory until you close the app, not on disk.
privacy.contacts.deezer: Deezer. To show photos of your artists, the names of the artists in your library are sent to Deezer. The photos are kept on your computer. You can turn this off in Settings, under Artist photos; photos that were downloaded stay. When you search for a photo yourself, the text you type is sent to Deezer too, and the pictures of the results are loaded from Deezer.
privacy.contacts.github: GitHub, for updates. The installer version looks for a new release on GitHub when it starts, which you can turn off in Settings. The Microsoft Store version never does that: the Store brings the updates.
privacy.nothingElse: Nothing else leaves your computer, and nothing is sent to the author of Tunelle. Your music files are never uploaded.
privacy.content.title: Where the content comes from
privacy.content.sources: Stations are listed by radio-browser.info, a community directory that anyone can add stations to. Tunelle does not run, check or endorse the stations or what they broadcast. The photos of artists belong to Deezer and to their rights holders, and covers from the Cover Art Archive belong to their rights holders, who uploaded them or whose work they show.
privacy.content.independent: Tunelle is an independent project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by radio-browser.info, Deezer, MusicBrainz or Microsoft. Their names belong to them.
privacy.station.title: A station you object to
privacy.station.text: Tunelle cannot remove a station from the directory. To report a station, use the report options of radio-browser.info. To tell us about a problem with the app, or with what it shows, open an issue.
privacy.contact.title: Contact
privacy.contact.text: Questions about this page: github.com/Koeroesi86/tunelle/issues. This page changes with the app, and its history is in the repository.
